territory: Ramsey Borough and Allendale Borough, Bergen County, New Jersey
summary:
I registered 14 records for Ramsey and Allendale, which is 13 distinct sources. Eight of them are programmatic and ready to use.

**Programmatic and clearly permitted (`tos_ok` = true):**
1. **NJGIN Parcels and MOD-IV Composite** is the parcel base. It gives block/lot, year built, values, last deed date and price, and owner mailing address. Owner names are redacted.
2. **NJ Division of Taxation MOD-IV annual files** give 2021–2026 snapshots, so you can see year-over-year changes.
3. **NJ SR1A Sales File** gives the date, price and usability code for each sale.
4. **NJ Construction Permit Data** is on data.nj.gov with a Socrata API and has block/lot permit history.
5. **FEMA National Flood Hazard Layer (NFHL) for NJ** gives flood zones.
6. **NJGIN orthoimagery** supports roof, tree and pool checks.
7. **NJ Building Footprints** gives structure sizes.
8. **Census ACS 5-year API** gives block-group priors for tenure, recent move-in, income and number of workers.
9. **NJDEP Land Use/Land Cover 2020** and **NJDEP Known Contaminated Site List** are lower-value context and exclusion layers.

**Manual or unverified (`tos_ok` = false):**
- **Allendale Maps page** links to a zoning map, tax maps and a GovPilot viewer. I found no API or bulk download.
- **Ramsey Building Department** has no open-data feed. Permits and certificates of compliance would come through an OPRA request.
- **NJ Clean Energy solar data** is unverified. I don't know the file format or whether it has address-level records.

**Caveats:**
- **Owner names:** I did not use any source to identify owners. The SR1A layout includes grantor and grantee name fields, and I couldn't confirm they are redacted. I registered the file only for sale date, price and usability code. Drop every name column when you load it. I could not verify how the MOD-IV annual files handle the owner-name field, so the same rule applies there. The Ramsey OPRA route should also exclude owner and contractor names.
- **Registry errors, which I could not delete:**
  - **Duplicate record:** the first Known Contaminated Sites entry was submitted without its notes and still registered. I re-submitted a complete one, so there are two records for that source. Please treat the first as void.
  - **Wrong district code:** the Construction Permit entry's note refers to "Bergen 0243-type district" for Ramsey. That was a guess and shouldn't be relied on.
  - **Unchecked coverage:** DCA says the permit feed covers most municipalities, not all. I haven't confirmed that Ramsey and Allendale are in it.
- **Search limit:** I ran out of search calls before checking some items:
  - Allendale's GovPilot terms.
  - Whether Ramsey has an online permit portal.
  - Bergen County's own GIS services.
  - The Census Geocoder, which would help match addresses to block groups.
- **Field lists:** The parcel field lists come from the NJGIN standard. Check them against the live schema before building on them.

**Gaps:** The data covers sale timing, owner-occupancy, and permit and tax history. It has no direct signal for dual-income households, so only the Census block-group priors apply there. Both boroughs are largely sewered, so I left out the septic/sewer layer.

--- earlier run ---
I registered 11 sources, which is below the 12–15 I hoped for. My search quota ran out partway through, so a few follow-ups remain unchecked.

**Core sources (open, programmatic access)**
1. **NJOGIS Parcels and MOD-IV, Bergen County download.** This is the base file. Filter to Ramsey and Allendale and to property class 2 to build the ~570-home list. It carries year built, land and improvement values, acreage, and sale fields.
2. **NJ Parcels and MOD-IV Composite, hosted ArcGIS feature service.** This is the same data through an API, so you can refresh it with a municipality filter.
3. **NJ DCA Construction Permit Data (data.nj.gov).** This is the statewide permit feed on the Socrata API. It is the best open source for recent roofing, HVAC, solar and renovation activity.
4. **ACS 5-Year via the Census API,** plus **5. NJOGIS Census Block Groups 2020.** Together they give neighborhood priors for dual-income households, owner-occupancy, move-in year and income. They are aggregates only.
6. **FEMA NFHL for NJ.** Flood zone by parcel centroid, for waterproofing and drainage leads.
7. **NJDEP Land Use/Land Cover 2020.** Coarse context such as wooded or wetland adjacency.
8. **NJ Clean Energy / Rutgers renewable energy reports.** I expect municipal- or ZIP-level adoption context only. I didn't confirm whether any address-level data exists.

**Sources that need a records request, not scraping**
9. **Ramsey Borough permits.** The site has a GovPilot forms portal but no data feed. Use an OPRA request for a permit log.
10. **Allendale Borough permits.** Same situation, using an OPRA request. Zoning permits for fences, driveways and dumpsters are useful project signals.
11. **Ramsey Ch. 34 and Allendale Ch. 270 zoning ordinances (eCode360).** These are reference text only. Read them by hand and ask each borough for its zoning map. I registered this one without an `icp_use` value, which the tool accepted.

**Caveats**
- **Owner names (Daniel's Law).** The county tax boards association (NJACTB) says it stopped serving the tax list and sales data (MOD-IV and SR1A) after Daniel's Law took effect. Before ingesting the NJOGIS files, check which owner-name and mailing-address fields are populated. Drop any owner-name column. Don't use mailing address to identify individuals. At most, use a mailing-versus-property address match as an owner-occupied flag.
- **Unverified details.** The MOD-IV field lists come from dataset descriptions plus my general knowledge, not a live schema check. I also didn't confirm whether the DCA permit data has parcel-level identifiers or how current Bergen's parcel vintage is.
- **Sales data.** Because of the NJACTB change, sale price and date may be thin or absent. If so, "recently moved" will depend on the sale fields in the NJOGIS files, the Census move-in-year priors, and permit timing.
- **Not registered.** I left out Zillow, Redfin and Realtor.com, and the third-party vendor Equator Studios (Bergen parcel and LiDAR downloads, not checked for terms or redundancy). I also left out the NJACTB record search because it is no longer available.
- **Still to check:** NJOGIS aerial imagery and building footprints (roof age and condition proxies), Bergen County GIS or open data, municipal zoning map files, and any code-enforcement data. I couldn't search these before the quota ran out.

sources.name: Parcels and MOD-IV Composite of NJ (statewide; filter MUN to Ramsey / Allendale)
sources.publisher: NJ Office of GIS (NJOGIS / NJGIN) with NJOIT/Treasury MOD-IV data
fields: owner mailing address/city/zip (owner NAME is redacted)
sources.join_key: block/lot (PAMS_PIN) - this is the master parcel spine; also address and lat/lng via polygon centroid
sources.tos_note: Public NJGIN open-data layer (hosted feature service plus download). Verified from NJGIN update log that owner names are redacted in the composite per Daniel's Law. Field list reflects the NJGIN parcel standard and should be confirmed against the live schema. Ramsey and Allendale are in Bergen County, so also available as the county-level Parcels and MOD-IV of Bergen County download.
sources.icp_use: Spine for every score. Filters to single-family (class 2 / building description) to define the ~570 homes. Year built and assessed value feed needs-services. Deed date and sale price feed recently moved. Comparing owner mailing address with property address gives owner-occupied vs absentee. Land and improvement value feed income/affluence proxies for hires-out.

sources.name: NJ Property Assessment List (MOD-IV) annual files
sources.publisher: NJ Division of Taxation, Local Property Tax
fields: owner mailing address (confirm owner-name handling in file)
sources.join_key: block/lot (district code + block + lot) or address
sources.tos_note: Official state statistical downloads, with published file layout and archived files for 2021 to 2026. I could not verify how the owner-name field is handled. Drop any name field at ingestion, and do not use this file to identify owners.
sources.icp_use: Year-over-year snapshots show change events: a new sale, a change in owner mailing address, or an improvement-value jump (renovation or addition). These support recently moved and needs services. Also a fallback and cross-check for the NJGIN composite.

sources.name: NJ Construction Permit Data (DCA monthly municipal reports)
sources.publisher: NJ Department of Community Affairs via NJOIT Open Data Center (data.nj.gov, Socrata dataset w9se-dmra)
sources.join_key: municipality code + block/lot
sources.tos_note: Open data with a Socrata SODA API and bulk CSV/XML download. DCA notes that data is collected from most, but not all, municipalities, so check that Ramsey (Bergen 0243-type district) and Allendale actually appear and how many months are lagged. Not owner-name data.
sources.icp_use: Needs services and hires out. Roof, HVAC, window, addition and remodel permits show homes that spend on contractors. A lack of recent permits on an older home suggests deferred maintenance. A new certificate of occupancy after a sale supports recently moved.

sources.name: National Flood Hazard Layer (NFHL) of New Jersey
sources.publisher: FEMA, hosted by NJDEP via ArcGIS Hub
sources.join_key: lat/lng (spatial join to parcel centroid or polygon)
sources.tos_note: Federal flood data, free and public, served as an ArcGIS feature layer. Regulatory FIRM data may lag newer NJDEP and FEMA updates. Use for risk flags, not insurance determinations.
sources.icp_use: Needs services. Homes in or near special flood hazard areas near the Ramsey brook corridors and Allendale low areas are more likely to need sump pumps, waterproofing, drainage, and mold remediation.

sources.name: NJGIN Orthoimagery (statewide aerial photography, downloads and web map service)
fields: web map/image service access via NJOGIS ArcGIS
sources.join_key: lat/lng (clip to parcel polygon)
sources.tos_note: State-published imagery with explicit download through the Imagery Warehouse and WMS access. Imagery will show a given home but contains no resident data. Any computer-vision outputs should stay property-level, not person-level.
sources.icp_use: Needs services. Roof condition and age proxy, tree canopy over roof, pool, deck and driveway presence, and lawn and yard size for lawn, tree, gutter, roofing and paving offers.

sources.name: Building Footprints of New Jersey
sources.publisher: NJ Office of GIS (NJGIN Open Data)
sources.join_key: lat/lng (spatial join to parcel polygon)
sources.tos_note: The BTAA geoportal entry points to the NJGIN open data portal layer. Verify the current endpoint on njogis-newjersey.opendata.arcgis.com, because the listing is dated 2019. Footprints will be missing for recent additions or rebuilds.
sources.icp_use: Needs services. Footprint area and building count per lot (garages and outbuildings) help size jobs such as roofing, siding, and gutters. Compared with MOD-IV dwelling size and recent permits, a footprint mismatch can reveal unpermitted or recent additions.

sources.name: American Community Survey 5-year API (block group / tract)
fields: workers per household, commute and employment tables (B23xxx, B08xxx)
sources.join_key: block group/tract (via lat/lng or the Census Geocoder)
sources.tos_note: Public Census Data API (a free key is recommended). Estimates are aggregate only and apply to the neighborhood, not to a specific household. Block-group margins of error can be large in small boroughs, so use them as priors, never as a statement about an individual home.
sources.icp_use: Neighborhood priors for dual-income (share of households with two or more workers, median income), recently moved (share who moved in during the last 5 years), and owner-occupied (tenure share). Used to calibrate the door-level score and break ties.

sources.name: Land Use/Land Cover of New Jersey 2020 (with impervious surface and tree canopy classes)
sources.join_key: lat/lng (spatial join to parcel polygon)
sources.tos_note: NJDEP open data (feature service and download). Polygon minimum mapping unit is coarse, so it is better for neighborhood-level context than for individual lots. Use the 2020 imagery for fine-grained lot detail.
sources.icp_use: Needs services. Wooded or high-canopy blocks suggest tree work, gutter cleaning and roof moss. Impervious share signals drainage and paving needs. Also confirms that parcels are low-density residential.

sources.name: NJDEP Known Contaminated Site List (KCSL)
fields: contaminant type (often petroleum, including residential heating-oil tanks)
sources.join_key: lat/lng (spatial join); address as fallback

sources.name: Allendale Borough Maps page (GovPilot map, zoning map, tax assessment maps)
sources.join_key: block/lot (from tax maps); zone labels need georeferencing
sources.tos_note: The page links to maps and viewers, but I found no published API or bulk download and did not review the terms. Treat as a manual reference for zoning districts (single-family zones). Do not scrape the GovPilot viewer. Ask the borough whether a zoning shapefile is available. District rules are in the borough's Chapter 270 on ecode360.
sources.icp_use: Confirms single-family zoning by parcel and flags lots in multi-family or townhouse zones to drop from the ~570 home list. Lot-size and setback rules help judge feasibility for additions.

sources.name: Ramsey Borough Building & Construction Department (permits, certificates of compliance, via OPRA)
fields: certificates of occupancy / compliance (required before home sale or rental per the borough FAQ)
sources.join_key: address; block/lot on request
sources.tos_note: No open-data feed was found. Access would be through a formal OPRA request for a permit log, which is a legitimate public-records route. Request only address/block/lot, permit type, date and value, and ask for owner, applicant and contractor-of-record names to be left out. Do not scrape any online permit portal without reviewing its terms.
sources.icp_use: Gives more current and complete permit history than the DCA monthly feed, and the certificate-of-compliance requirement on sale or rental gives a recently-moved timestamp. It also covers needs services and hires-out signals.

sources.name: NJ Clean Energy Program renewable energy / solar installation data
sources.publisher: NJ Board of Public Utilities / Rutgers Energy Data
fields: installation records by program (REIP, CORE, SREC registration)
sources.join_key: municipality/ZIP; address only if the files include it (unverified)
sources.tos_note: The Rutgers page describes public project activity reports and the program data. I did not verify the file formats, license, or whether address-level records exist, so keep this unapproved until checked. Do not use any customer-name fields.
sources.icp_use: Needs services and hires out. Homes with existing solar are likely candidates for roof work, monitoring, and electrical add-ons, and a good proxy for homeowners who hire contractors.

sources.name: Parcels and MOD-IV of Bergen County, NJ (shapefile/FGDB download)
sources.publisher: NJ Office of GIS (NJOGIS / NJGIN) with NJ Division of Taxation MOD-IV
fields: last sale date/price/deed fields (verify present after Daniel's Law changes)
sources.join_key: block/lot (PAMS_PIN <-> GIS_PIN); parcel polygons give lat/lng
sources.tos_note: Public NJOGIS open data download. Spine dataset: filter to Ramsey and Allendale and property class 2 to get the ~570 SFH universe. Field list is from the dataset descriptions plus my general knowledge of MOD-IV, not a schema check, so confirm the live schema. NJACTB has stopped serving MOD-IV and SR1A since Daniel's Law. Check whether owner-name fields are now blank or redacted, and do not use any that are populated.
sources.icp_use: owner-occupied (mailing vs. situs address match), recently moved (sale date), home age/value/size for needs-services and hires-out proxies

sources.name: Parcels and MOD-IV Composite of NJ (hosted ArcGIS feature service, Web Mercator)
fields: joined MOD-IV attributes (class, year built, assessed values, building description, acreage, sale fields)
sources.join_key: block/lot / PAMS_PIN; geometry gives lat/lng
sources.tos_note: Public ArcGIS REST service on NJ's open data hub. Use it for incremental pulls with a where-clause on municipality, instead of downloading the full county file. The statewide composite is updated county by county, so check the update log for Bergen's vintage. Same owner-field caveat as the county download.
sources.icp_use: same as county download; API-friendly route for refreshing parcel and tax attributes (owner-occupied, recently moved)

sources.name: American Community Survey 5-Year (block group / tract) via Census API
fields: households with two or more workers
sources.join_key: block group / tract (via lat/lng or GEOID spatial join)
sources.tos_note: Free public API (api.census.gov), with an API key recommended. It is aggregate data only, so use it as a neighborhood prior and never as a per-household attribute. Block-group margins of error are large; Ramsey and Allendale have only a few dozen block groups between them.
sources.icp_use: dual-income (multi-worker household share), hires out (income/age/education priors), recently moved (move-in year distribution), owner-occupied

sources.name: Census Block Groups 2020 (Hosted, NJ State Plane)
sources.publisher: NJ Office of GIS (from U.S. Census TIGER/Line)
sources.join_key: lat/lng point-in-polygon, then GEOID to ACS
sources.tos_note: Public-domain Census geography republished on NJ's open data hub. Used only to attach parcels to ACS block groups.
sources.icp_use: geographic bridge from parcel centroid to ACS demographics (dual-income, owner-occupied, recently moved priors)

sources.name: National Flood Hazard Layer (NFHL) of New Jersey
sources.join_key: lat/lng (parcel centroid point-in-polygon)
sources.tos_note: Federal flood map data, publicly available through FEMA and the state ArcGIS hub. Both boroughs have stream corridors (the Ramapo River and Saddle River areas), so a minority of parcels should fall in flood zones.
sources.icp_use: needs services (basement waterproofing, sump pumps, drainage, gutters, mold remediation)

sources.name: Ramsey Borough Construction Department - permit records (OPRA request) and online forms
sources.join_key: address or block/lot
sources.tos_note: Permits are issued through the Construction Department, and forms run through a GovPilot eForms portal. I found no open permit data feed. The compliant route is a formal OPRA request for a permit log covering residential permits in a date range, not scraping the portal. Ask for the log without applicant or owner names, and ask for property address, permit type, and issue date.
sources.icp_use: needs services and recently moved (hyper-local permit history that the state feed may lack); hires out (prior contractor-performed work)

sources.name: Allendale Borough Construction & Zoning permits - permit records (OPRA request)
sources.join_key: address or block/lot
sources.tos_note: The site publishes permit forms, not permit data. Get records through an OPRA request to the Construction Department. Request address, permit type, and date only, with no owner or applicant names. Zoning permits (fence, driveway, dumpster) are a good activity signal that the state DCA feed will not capture.
sources.icp_use: needs services (fence, driveway, dumpster, and renovation permits show active projects); recently moved

sources.name: Municipal zoning ordinances - Ramsey Ch. 34 and Allendale Ch. 270 (eCode360)
sources.publisher: Borough of Ramsey / Borough of Allendale via General Code eCode360
fields: zoning district regulations (lot size, setbacks, coverage)
permit requirements for fences, driveways, additions
sources.join_key: none (district from municipal zoning map; no parcel-level data feed found)
sources.tos_note: Reference text only. I found no machine-readable zoning layer, so do not bulk-scrape eCode360. Read it manually to understand which residential zones apply, and ask each borough for its zoning map shapefile or PDF. The zone could then be assigned to parcels by overlay. No owner data is involved.
